cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Credit for the Discovery
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you found the clue, saw through the deception, or designed the successful scheme.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll start tomorrow's house tour at the hidden doorway. Say my diagram revealed it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum spent all week stripping that wall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll credit her work first. Then say who spotted the door before she stripped the wall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll let you open it for the visitors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll open it. Introduce me as the one who found it, though, or they'll just thank me for holding it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs the tour start and credit; A3 grants Mum first labor recognition; A5 accepts B opening role only with an introduction preserving A discovery identity.

responseLogic.evidence: A1 diagram discovery and B2 later wall stripping are compatible, and A3 explicitly distinguishes finding from exposing the doorway.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects Mum work and B4 offers A a visible role that B thinks provides recognition.

heightening.evidence: B4 door-opening role could make A look merely helpful, so A5 demands finder introduction; the offered solution creates the next credit problem.

specificity.evidence: A1 house tour, hidden doorway and diagram make both practical task and desired acknowledgment specific.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 acceptance, requested introduction and mistaken-door-holder risk are all tied to B4 actual offer.
